chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn; and Ḥabīb ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-ʿAṭṭār, from Yasār, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The sorcerer is struck with the sword, one single blow upon his head.”

key_terms.يُضْرَبُ: is to be struck or executed

ai.seo_question: What punishment does the hadith in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām prescribe for the sorcerer?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the punishment of the sorcerer. It presents the ruling in brief and emphatic language, indicating a fixed judicial penalty within the context of criminal law.
